Definition: from the same as G3013; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy":--leprosy.
BiblicalUsage: lépra means leprosy, and it does large work in the story. In Matthew 8:3, "And immediately his leprosy was cleansed."; and in Mark 1:42, "immediately the leprosy departed from him". In Luke 5:12, "behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on [his] face"; and in Luke 5:13, "And immediately the leprosy departed from him.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe leprosy is sin made visible — the man full of leprosy fell on his face, and Jesus touched him and said He would make him clean. I hold that no disease is too defiling for that touch, and no sinner too far gone for that word. My position is that I come to Him as the leper came: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
